newsitem.title: USA: Amax Gold Fort Knox to reach 300,000oz in 97.
newsitem.headline: Amax Gold Fort Knox to reach 300,000oz in 97.

text.p: Production at Amax Gold's new, wholly-owned $370 million Fort Knox gold mine will be 300,000 ounces this year, said Milton Ward, Chairman, President and CEO of Cyprus Amax Minerals which owns some 60 percent of the yellow metal producer.
"We expect that Fort Knox in 1997 will produce, even though it's a start up year, about 300,000 ounces of gold," Ward told an analysts teleconference Thursday.
"We have shown the operation is viable," Ward added.

Amax Gold produced 103,000 ounces in the first quarter, up 75 percent from the same quarter last year as Fort Knox ramped up, along with the Refugio project in Chile in which Amax has a 50 percent stake.
"This is a dramatic increase and it's going to increase more as the year progresses," Ward said.
"We will be at 700,000 ounces (Amax output rate) by the end of the year," Ward added.
Cash costs were cut by 21 percent to $236 an ounce in the first quarter when gold earned $1 million compared to a $2 million loss in the same period last year.
Gold spot prices averaged $351 per ounce during the first quarter when the company's average realised price was $388 per ounce, down from $412 last year.
Start-up of Amax's 50-percent owned Kubaka operation in Russia is proceeding well after the first gold pour in February with commercial production beginning mid-year, Ward said.
Reserves at Fort Knox were also expected to be raised. "We are finding more gold there," Ward said.
Ward said Cyprus was still talking with other companies about merging with Amax Gold. "I want to get that done before the end of the year," Ward said.
A merger would lead to a better financial situation for Amax Gold, restructure its finances and help tackle high debts, Cyprus official said.
Amax still had a "vigorous" hedging program in place.
"If the market stays at $350 an ounce, we will net $380 an ounce or a little higher for the rest of the year," Cyprus Amax's senior vice president and CFO Gerald Malys said.
But this would still not be enough to pay off interest on Amax Gold's debts, Malys added.
Ward said much of Cyprus Amax's exploration will yield results in gold rather than copper, with a push to convert gold resources into reserves.
